name: Khashm el Girba sorghum with domestication traits
description: Sorghum plant remains embedded in pottery from Khashm el Girba 23 in eastern Sudan include both non-shattering and wild-type forms, evidence of human selection in an early crop.

impact.note: One site's early evidence of sorghum under human selection; a new ability locally, on the line leading to domesticated sorghum.

date.label: Approximately 3900–2500 calibrated BCE (95.4% ranges)
date.basis: The paper reports broad two-sigma calibrated ranges for wood charcoal at the site, rounded to centuries; its narrower 3700–2900 BCE interpretation uses one-sigma ranges.

events.statement: Sorghum plant remains embedded in pottery from Khashm el Girba 23 in eastern Sudan include both non-shattering and wild-type forms, evidence of human selection in an early crop.
events.caveats: The broader two-sigma charcoal ranges are uncertain and may be affected by old wood. The 3700–2900 BCE range used by the authors is one sigma; the original location and timing of cultivation are unknown.

evidence.supports: The site yielded mixed sorghum morphologies; the authors report approximately 73% non-shattering among identifiable specimens and a 3700–2900 BC contextual chronology.

earliest_record.rationale: The site context is dated using broad charcoal ranges, not a direct date of the plant impressions or the beginning of selection.

caveats: The broader two-sigma charcoal ranges are uncertain and may be affected by old wood. The 3700–2900 BCE range used by the authors is one sigma; the original location and timing of cultivation are unknown.

research.note: Independent check of the cited passages and marked facets on 2026-11-09; interpretations and date limits retain the stated caveats.

measures.quantity: Non-shattering share of identifiable spikelet-base visualizations
measures.conditions: 57 of 78 identifiable sorghum spikelet-base visualizations (about 73%) from the sampled KG23 pottery. The authors use a 3700–2900 BCE one-sigma context; broader two-sigma charcoal ranges are approximately 3900–2500 BCE. This sample is not a field-wide crop proportion.

evidence.supports: Reports approximately 73% non-shattering and 27% wild-type among identifiable visualizations.

measures.subject: MicroCT classifications of sorghum spikelet bases in sampled KG23 pottery
measures.denominator_definition: Spikelet bases classified as either domesticated or wild among MicroCT visualizations of sampled KG23 pottery; excludes indeterminate visualizations. This is an archaeological specimen sample, not people, fields, or adoption.
measures.method: 57 divided by 78, multiplied by 100 and rounded to the nearest whole percent.
